stories.title: TNFD calls on ISSB to upgrade nature guidance to a standard
stories.summary: The Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures wants the International Sustainability Standards Board to replace its draft nature Practice Statement with a full Standard. The proposal includes a small set of required cross-sector metrics. Responses to the request are due by 19 February 2027.

stories.title: Productivity Commission recommends non-financial reporting be simplified - HR Leader
Amalgamated Bank appoints Sean Wright as chief sustainability officer
stories.summary: Amalgamated Bank has appointed Sean Wright as its new chief sustainability officer. Wright, previously the head of climate transition at Morgan Stanley, succeeds Ivan Frishberg. The bank says the move is part of a long-planned leadership transition to advance its climate and sustainable finance priorities.

stories.title: KPIT Technologies gets SBTi validation for net-zero emissions targets by FY50 - ET Auto
Stibbe contributes to Chambers Global Practice Guide on ESG
stories.summary: Branda Katan, Valérie van ‘t Lam, Heleen Kersten and Marieke Driessen contributed to the Chambers Global Practice Guide: ESG 2026. Their chapter covers law and practice in the Netherlands, including developments in sustainable finance, transparency, reporting and climate litigation. The guide provides an overview of current trends.

stories.title: Summit Hotel Properties expands ESG reporting to include resilience
stories.summary: Summit Hotel Properties has released its 2026 Corporate Responsibility Report, covering 92 hotels and 14,027 guestrooms. The lodging REIT has added resilience as a fourth pillar alongside environmental, social and governance frameworks. Previous reports focused primarily on property-level utility monitoring and efficiency programs.

stories.title: California ruling raises doubts over Scope 3 reporting across US - Sustainable Views
Shinhan Financial Group wins sustainability reporting award
stories.summary: Shinhan Financial Group has received the Korea Sustainability Reporting Award for the seventh consecutive year. The group was recognized at the 2026 Korea Sustainability Conference for its efforts in transparently disclosing management achievements. This marks the group's 11th win overall since its induction into the Hall of Fame.

stories.title: Grand Korea Leisure sustainability report wins platinum award
stories.summary: Grand Korea Leisure scored 99 out of 100 in an international competition, earning a platinum award at the 2025/26 LACP Spotlight Awards. The company, which operates the Seven Luck casino, achieved perfect marks in five of the six evaluation categories among more than 500 participating organizations.

stories.title: EU and UK reach agreement on carbon market linkage
stories.summary: The European Union and the UK have concluded negotiations to link their emissions trading systems, aiming for implementation on 1 January 2028. While some industry actors welcome the cooperation, others, including UK manufacturer Ineos, have expressed concerns regarding potential financial burdens.

stories.title: COP31 concludes without climate pact
stories.summary: The COP31 summit in Antalya ended without a wider climate agreement as disputes over fossil fuels and carbon capture targets blocked consensus. The event highlighted a funding gap for carbon removal technologies, leaving countries in disagreement over how to scale and pay for these solutions.

stories.title: Ghana earns 6.5 million forest carbon credits under international scheme - Asaase Radio
Article 6 negotiations stall at COP31
stories.summary: Negotiators at COP31 held an Article 6.2 Ambition Dialogue to discuss the authorization of carbon credits for international transfer. The market faces a supply shortage as participants struggle to price the risk associated with credits that are now considered project assets wrapped in sovereign decisions.

stories.title: Ghana forest carbon credits could generate $68 million
stories.summary: Ghana's forest carbon credit program is projected to generate $68 million from 6.5 million credits. According to the reported figures, 46 percent of the revenue is allocated to local communities. The project remains part of ongoing discussions regarding national carbon credit management.

stories.title: MMCM issues first carbon credits from vehicle scrapping
stories.summary: Meta Materials Circular Markets has issued 24,988 carbon credits derived from end-of-life vehicle recycling in India. The company operates a program with registered scrapping facilities to provide incentives for formal recycling. These are the first carbon credits issued from vehicle scrapping operations.

stories.title: China to join CORSIA from 2027
stories.summary: China has confirmed it will participate in the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation from 2027 to 2029. The government will retain approval authority over the carbon offset products used by Chinese airlines, as global demand for aviation credits continues to rise.

stories.title: EU pushes methane rules for fuel importers back to 2030
stories.summary: EU countries and the European Parliament have agreed to delay parts of the EU Methane Regulation by two years. Importers now have until May 2030 to prove contract compliance, with reporting requirements also pushed back. The delay is attributed to energy market disruption linked to the US-Israeli war.

stories.title: Visegrad Group leaders demand ETS2 delay to 2030 - Euronews.com
Prime Minister pledges UK climate leadership at G20
stories.summary: Following the failure to deliver a new accord at COP31, the Prime Minister has promised to use the UK's upcoming G20 presidency to rebuild global leadership on climate. The government described the recent international climate summit as deeply disappointing.

stories.title: Government confirms UK heatwave death toll exceeded 5,000
stories.summary: Latest government figures indicate that the death toll from UK summer heatwaves reached its highest level since monitoring began in 2016. Officials confirmed the mortality data, noting the trend is not a freak accident.

stories.title: Nature groups warn against dismantling environmental regulators
stories.summary: The RSPB, National Trust, Wildlife Trusts, and Woodland Trust have warned that moving Natural England to a quango bonfire would be a costly mistake. The organizations are calling for regulators to be empowered to drive investment in critical natural infrastructure rather than being dissolved or devolved.

stories.title: Whitehall considers overhaul of environmental regulators
stories.summary: Ministers are considering the dissolution or devolution of bodies like the Environment Agency and Natural England as part of a wider state overhaul. Conservation leaders have condemned the move as an ideological crusade, while ministers insist that decisions must sit closer to the communities they affect.

stories.title: Twenty councils scrap net zero targets
stories.summary: Climate Emergency UK reports that 20 councils have scrapped net zero targets since 2025, while 28 have strengthened theirs. The data highlights a postcode lottery for climate action, with some administrations cutting funding for initiatives like electric vehicle charging points to prioritize other local goals.

stories.title: COP31 places food security at center of climate talks
stories.summary: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya focused on global agrifood systems as temperatures track toward an overshoot of the 1.5C threshold. For India, where agriculture sustains 45 percent of the workforce, the outcomes carry significant economic implications following the failure to reach a new accord.

stories.title: COP31 talks conclude without major agreement
stories.summary: Geopolitical fractures over fossil fuels and finance thwarted consensus on the main cover decision at COP31. While the Antalya Pact failed to materialize, delegates managed to navigate 165 other agenda items. The conference ended with the same divisions that defined the start of the talks.

stories.title: Kithul tappers face challenges in global market expansion
stories.summary: Wimalasiri, a kithul tapper in Suriyakanda, harvests sap using traditional methods and bamboo ladders. While the work is physically demanding, experts suggest that better technology and increased investment could transform livelihoods and help these traditional producers reach global markets.

stories.title: Joint Innovation Facility launches circularity call for 2027
stories.summary: The Joint Innovation Facility is inviting African businesses in waste management and recycling to partner with European firms. The initiative aims to develop commercially viable joint ventures and scale sustainable business solutions across East and Southern Africa through the 2027 Circularity Call.

stories.title: New Mexico awards $11.5 million for circular economy projects
stories.summary: The New Mexico Environment Department has selected 15 projects to receive $11.5 million to advance circular economy practices. The funding supports initiatives including the recycling of wind turbine blades and solar panels, aiming to reduce pollution and strengthen local supply chains.

stories.title: Hong Kong shifts focus to waste-to-resources
stories.summary: Aligned with the national 15th Five-Year Plan, Hong Kong is advancing a 2035 waste-to-resources vision. The city aims to treat waste as a productive asset rather than a management expense, focusing on capital efficiency and long-term value creation to drive green transformation.

stories.title: Circular Economy Act delayed, again - Plastics News
Amended law targets electronic waste management
stories.summary: The 16th National Assembly has passed an amended Environmental Protection Law, effective March 1, 2027. The legislation aims to reduce pollution from electronic waste, which contributes 70 percent of toxins to landfills despite representing only 2 percent of household waste.

stories.title: DITF launches recycling center for textile industry
stories.summary: The German Institutes of Textile and Fiber Research has established the CYCLOTEXUM recycling center to develop mechanical and solvent-based recycling processes. Funded by the state of Baden-Wurttemberg, the project aims to transition the German textile sector toward a circular economy.

stories.title: Wind industry reports increase in blade recycling
stories.summary: New data from WindEurope shows that 97 percent of reported wind turbine blade waste was diverted from landfill in 2025. This represents an increase from 89 percent in 2024 and 70 percent in previous years.

stories.title: Octavius wins environmental awards for infrastructure projects
stories.summary: Octavius received a Gold award for its Carbon Lite initiative and a commendation for its Circular Economy by Boat project at the 2026 Green Apple Environment Awards. The company was recognized for its efforts to minimize the environmental impact of essential transport infrastructure.

stories.title: Westlake releases ninth annual sustainability report
stories.summary: Westlake Corporation has released its ninth annual sustainability report. After achieving a 20 percent reduction in emissions per ton of production from a 2016 baseline, the company has committed to a further 5 percent reduction by 2030. The company remains deeply committed to sustainability.

stories.title: Indian Oil targets 31 GW renewable capacity
stories.summary: Indian Oil plans to invest up to 10,000 crore annually to reach 31 GW of renewable capacity within five years. The state-run refiner intends to use a 75 to 25 debt-equity ratio for its subsidiary, Terra Clean, to fund the expansion through acquisitions and joint ventures.

stories.title: Google signs 50-MW superhot geothermal PPA
stories.summary: Google has signed a power purchase agreement with Quaise Energy for 50 MW of superhot geothermal energy. The deal is intended to support the company's Oregon data center operations starting as early as 2030, using technology designed to access geothermal resources deeper underground.

stories.title: Amazon plans additional 7 billion dollar investment in India
stories.summary: Amazon announced plans to invest an additional 7 billion dollars in Indian renewable energy projects by 2030. The company unveiled four new wind and solar developments with a combined capacity of 934 MW, including what it describes as its largest wind project in Asia to date.

stories.title: Amazon aims to reduce carbon emissions 65 percent by 2030
stories.summary: Amazon has set a target to reduce carbon emissions for every unit of electricity it uses by 65 percent by 2030. The company has invested in over 7,000 projects globally, claiming enough capacity to power 12.1 million US homes once completed. The goal follows the net-zero pathway.

stories.title: Sterling and Wilson secures 600 MWh battery storage project
stories.summary: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy has secured three domestic orders valued at over 2,050 crore. The contracts include a 600 MWh battery energy storage system in Gujarat and 350 MW of solar capacity across Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. The company emerged as the lowest bidder for one project.

stories.title: NLC India plans 1.5 lakh crore investment by 2032
stories.summary: NLC India Limited plans to invest 1.5 lakh crore by 2032 to expand its renewable capacity to 16 GW and thermal capacity to 15 GW. The state-run company intends to increase its renewable footprint ninefold from its current capacity of 1,783.96 MW over the next eight years.

stories.title: NLC India plans ₹1.5 lakh crore capex push by 2032, targets 32 GW power capacity: CMD - Moneycontrol.com
Meta reconsiders net zero goal after emissions spike
stories.summary: Meta is re-evaluating its 2030 net zero target following a 45 percent increase in greenhouse gas emissions. The company attributed the rise to its accelerating AI infrastructure buildout, which it says is arriving on a timeline measured in quarters rather than decades. Progress has been adjusted.

research.title: Delhi’s rural outskirts are more polluted than the megacity, and crop burning is not the culprit
research.summary: This counter-intuitive phenomenon is driven by the high use of wood, dung and other household fuels for cooking and heating, a study finds. Delhi’s rural outskirts are more polluted than the megacity, and crop burning is not the culprit

research.summary: Nature India, Published online: 23 November 2026, doi:10.1038/d44151-026-00227-1 Olive Ridley hatchlings is the Rushikulya rookery get entrapped in nets and debris. Plastic litter kills baby turtles in major nesting site

research.title: A Comparison of Uncertainty in AI and Dynamical Climate Ensembles
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Climate model ensembles and their uncertainty estimates are essential for evaluating risk and designing climate policy. Yet, in the assessment of newly developed AI climate models, evaluating uncertainty is often secondary to diagnosing mean-state climate biases. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: A Fitch-Based Wind Farm Parameterization for CM1: Implementation, Validation, and Impacts on Convection Initiation
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: We implement a Fitch-based wind farm parameterization in Cloud Model 1 (CM1), representing turbines as elevated momentum sinks and turbulent kinetic energy (TKE) sources within the rotor-swept layer, with optimizations for computational efficiency and parallel execution. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: A Station-Based Evaluation of Machine Learning-based Weather Forecasting Models in Northern Norway
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent machine learning weather prediction (MLWP) models have demonstrated remarkable forecasting skill on global reanalysis-based benchmarks. However, their performance remains unclear in challenging environments such as Northern Norway, where narrow fjords and rapidly changing weather result. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: A high-order IMEX-DG solver for atmospheric dynamics: rotating tests on non-conforming meshes
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a high-order implicit-explicit discontinuous Galerkin (IMEX-DG) solver for the compressible Euler equations that accounts for rotational effects within an atmospheric framework. Time integration follows a second-order additive Runge-Kutta scheme, treating stiff acoustic modes implicitly. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: A multi-physics Eulerian framework for long-term contrail evolution (MultiCon): Single plume analysis
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present MultiCon, a reduced order, multi-physics Eulerian framework for simulating long term evolution of individual aircraft contrail plumes while retaining essential microphysical processes at low computational cost. The model resolves vertical plume evolution through a. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: An exact and differentiable rewrite of a coupled weather and fire model
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: AI is changing weather and climate prediction by replacing physical models with learned ones. Here we show a different path, in which AI coding agents rebuild the physical model itself in a machine-learning framework and reproduce. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
